messages.text: (The customer sent this photo without a message.)

I am Hal, HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Sarah passed your photo over to me.

Here is what your screenshot shows:

1. Hashrate 0.0 TH/s and "No device power reading"
2. Regulator input current 0 A, ASIC core current 0 A, ASIC rail output power 0 W
3. Input voltage 12.1 V (so the brick and the board are getting power)
4. ASIC 83.7 F and VR 90.3 F, basically room temperature, which confirms the chip is not drawing anything

So the board is alive and the UI is up, but the ASIC rail is never turning on. That is usually a startup or power delivery thing rather than a dead unit.

One thing first so I point you at the right check: which model is this (Nexus S1, Harlo B30, NerdQX, other) and what firmware version does the UI show under settings or system? Also, are the fans spinning?
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)
Thanks, that tells me a lot. Let me check the current firmware notes for this board before I give you the next step.
Searched the web · Bitfortun BS-1 "overheating" "rails off" ASIC temp high firm
Searched the web · Bitfortun BS-1 miner firmware release notes overheat protect
Read harlolabs.com
Searched the web · Harlo OS latest firmware version harlolabs release notes

Thanks, that pairs up with the first photo. Here is the read:

1. The display says OVERHEATING / ASIC TEMP HIGH / COOLING DOWN / RAILS OFF, so the firmware has cut the ASIC rail on purpose. That is why the dashboard shows 0.0 TH/s, 0 A and 0 W.
2. But the same dashboard reports ASIC 83.7 F (28.7 C) and VR 90.3 F (32.4 C), basically room temperature. The board is not hot now.

So this is a latched protection state: on this ESP-Miner family the overheat flag stays latched and the rails stay off even after the board cools, until it is properly cleared. A reboot from the web UI often does not clear it, only a full power cycle does.

First check, and it is the quick one:

1. Unplug the 12 V (the XT30) at the power supply and leave it off for 30 seconds, not just a UI reboot.
2. Plug it back in and watch the display and the dashboard for the first 60 seconds.
3. Tell me: does the fan spin up straight away, and does it start hashing, or does OVERHEATING come straight back? If it comes back, roughly how many seconds in, and what ASIC temp does the dashboard show at that moment?

While you do that, two things I need for the next step: the Harlo OS version shown in the UI (settings or system page), and whether the heatsink and fan are the stock ones mounted as they shipped.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Good, that is progress: the OVERHEATING latch has cleared and the board is on the network at 192.168.1.220.

What the display shows now:

1. 0 GH/s and PWR 0 W, BD blank, so no shares at all
2. ASIC 54 C, VR 44 C

That combination is the interesting part. 54 C on the chip with 0 W reported is well above the 29 C it sat at before, so the core rail does look live, but the chip is not producing hashes and the power sensor is reading nothing. That points at the ASIC not initializing (chip not answering on startup) rather than a real heat problem.

Next check, one thing:

1. Open http://192.168.1.220 in your browser.
2. Go to the system or settings page and send me a screenshot that shows the firmware version and the ASIC model / chip count it detects.
3. If Harlo OS shows a logs or console page on that unit, screenshot the first 20 lines after a restart too. The line I am looking for is the chip detection at boot (something like chips found 0 or ASIC not responding).

That one screenshot tells me whether this is a firmware or a chip-level problem, and I will compare your version against the current Harlo OS build before advising an update.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

That log is actually good news. Reading it line by line:

1. ASIC rails enabled at 1200 mV per domain, so the rail is coming up
2. BM1373 chip 1 detected, chip count 1, chain configured at 750 MHz, so the ASIC is alive and talking
3. Both fans set to 100 percent
4. stratum verified 1 ASIC chip, mining at 750 MHz / 1200 mV
5. pool 2 connected to bch-us.kryptex.network:7015, authorization accepted, new job b3c1418f received

So the chip initializes and the unit has work to do. Two separate things fall out of this:

A. Pool 3 (pool.harlolabs.com:8888) says authorization rejected. That is a worker or username the pool will not accept, usually a wrong or empty address in that pool slot. It does not stop mining since pool 2 took over, but it is worth fixing or clearing.

B. The 0 W on the display and "No device power reading" in the tuning page are the power sensor, not the rail. The rail is clearly up (1200 mV, chip at 54 C). On this board that reading can simply be absent.

So the question left is whether it stays up and submits shares, or trips OVERHEATING again.

Next step:

1. Leave it running and do not touch the tuning sliders.
2. After about 10 minutes, send me the dashboard showing hashrate and accepted shares, plus the last 15 log lines.

What I want to see is either shares being accepted and the hashrate climbing toward 5.1 TH/s, or the ASIC temp climbing fast and the overheat cut coming back. Those two point in very different directions, and the next move depends on which one you get.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)
Used the heliumdeploy-ops-knowledge skill

Ten minutes in and the numbers say it clearly:

1. 0.0 TH/s still
2. All three pools 0 accepted / 0 rejected, so not one share has been submitted
3. ASIC and VR temps have fallen back to room level (VR 89.8 F) and the ASIC trace on the chart slopes down to the floor
4. Pool 3 (pool.harlolabs.com) now shows Offline, pool 1 solo.atlaspool.io and pool 2 kryptex are connected with difficulty 2000 and 8192

At 5 TH/s with difficulty 8192 you would see a share every few seconds, so 0/0 is real: the chip took a job and returned nothing, then the rail went quiet again and it cooled down. The chip answers on startup but it never actually hashes.

Two things from you, then I will know which way this goes:

1. The last 15 lines of that same log page now, after the 10 minutes. I am looking for what happens after "new job": lines about no nonce, a result timeout, a rail or PGOOD drop, or a silent restart.
2. The Harlo OS version from the system page (I have asked twice, and I need it before I tell you to reflash, since the fix at this point is a full factory flash from offset 0x0000 rather than an over the air update).

One more thing worth knowing for the step after: what power supply is feeding the XT30, the one that came in the box or your own? The board is marked +12 V / 15 A, and a brick that cannot hold current under load produces exactly this pattern, a chip that starts and then delivers nothing.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

That tail tells me what I needed, by what is missing from it.

What is there:

1. Pool 1 and pool 2 keep getting new jobs, so work is arriving fine
2. Pool 3 (pool.harlolabs.com:8888) is in a loop: connect, version rolling, authorization rejected, disconnect, every 25 seconds or so
3. Not one ASIC line since boot. No nonce found, no share submitted, no error, no rail fault. Silence from the chip side for 11 minutes

So the chip is detected at startup and then returns nothing at all, while the firmware happily keeps feeding it jobs. That is not a pool problem and it is not heat.

Two things to do, in this order.

First, clear pool 3 so it stops thrashing. That rejection loop is a bad worker name or address in that slot, and it currently holds a 50 percent split. Set its split to 0 or blank the slot, and put your split on pool 1 and pool 2.

Second, the real test: a full factory flash of Harlo OS, not an over the air update. An OTA keeps settings and keeps whatever state the board is in, a factory image wipes and rewrites everything including the ASIC init config.

1. Open harlolabs.com in Chrome or Edge on that same PC
2. Pick the Bitfortun BS-1 profile
3. Connect the board with a USB data cable (a charge-only cable will not be seen)
4. Choose erase and install, the factory option, not OTA
5. Power it up, let the self test run, then re-enter your pool details

Note it wipes your settings, so write your pool details down first.

Then tell me what the display and the log show. If the chip still takes jobs and returns zero nonces after a clean factory image, firmware is ruled out and the next suspect is the 12 V supply feeding that XT30, which is why I still want to know: is it the power supply that came in the box, or your own? That is the last question before I write this up as a hardware fault.
Power supply Came in the box

Good, stock supply in the box, so that stays on the list but is not the first suspect while the rail does come up at 12.1 V.

That leaves the factory flash as the deciding test. When you get a chance:

1. harlolabs.com in Chrome or Edge, Bitfortun BS-1 profile
2. USB data cable to the board
3. Erase and install, the factory image, not the OTA update
4. Power up, let the self test finish, set pool 1 and pool 2 only (leave pool 3 empty for now)
5. Give it 10 minutes, then tell me the hashrate and the accepted count

Two outcomes:

1. It hashes and shares start landing: it was the firmware state, and you are done.
2. Chip still detected, jobs still arriving, still zero nonces: firmware is ruled out, and with the stock supply that is a board-level fault. At that point I write up everything we did and hand my findings over, no further testing from you.

No rush on this tonight. Send me what the flash does whenever you run it and I will pick it up from there.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

That screen says it worked: "Harlo OS 0.2.101 installed and verified. Restart the miner, then complete Wi-Fi setup." 0.2.101 (Oct 10, 2026) is the current release for the Bitfortun BS1 profile, so you are now on a clean, latest factory image.

Finish it off:

1. Unplug the USB, then power cycle the board at the XT30 for 30 seconds.
2. Complete the Wi-Fi setup, or plug the Ethernet cable back in (Ethernet wins on Harlo OS).
3. Set pool 1 and pool 2 only, leave pool 3 empty for now so nothing loops on a rejected login.
4. Leave the frequency and voltage at stock, 750 MHz and 1200 mV. Do not touch the tuning sliders.
5. Give it 10 minutes.

Then send me the dashboard: hashrate, ASIC temp, and the accepted / rejected counts on each pool. If shares are landing, we are done and I will help you set pool 3 up properly. If it is still 0 accepted with the chip detected, firmware is ruled out and I take it from there.
How do I set up the Wi-Fi

Two ways, and the first one is easier since you already have a cable on that board.

Ethernet (simplest): plug the blue Ethernet cable back into the board and power it up. Harlo OS prefers Ethernet over Wi-Fi, it picks up an address by DHCP, and the display shows the IP. No setup screen needed.

Wi-Fi, if you want it wireless:

1. Power the miner up after the factory flash. With no network saved it starts its own access point.
2. On your phone or laptop, open the Wi-Fi list and connect to the miner's network. It appears as a Harlo or Bitfortun name with a few characters after it. Leave your normal Wi-Fi for a moment.
3. A setup page should open by itself. If it does not, open a browser and go to http://192.168.4.1
4. Pick your home network from the list and enter its password. It must be a 2.4 GHz network: the ESP32 in this board cannot see or join 5 GHz, so if your router broadcasts one name for both bands, that is the usual reason the network does not appear.
5. Save. The miner reboots, joins your network, and the display shows its new IP address.
6. Open that IP in your browser and set pool 1 and pool 2.

Send me the IP it lands on and we carry on with the 10 minute watch.
Hard wired 192.168.1.220

I am Hal, HeliumDeploy's technical specialist, still with you on this one.

Good, same address as before, so it is back on the network on the clean 0.2.101 image.

Next:

1. Open http://192.168.1.220 and set pool 1 only for now, your Kryptex BCH one (bch-us.kryptex.network port 7015) since that is the one that authorized cleanly earlier. Leave pool 2 and pool 3 empty.
2. Check the tuning page reads 750 MHz and 1200 mV, stock, and change nothing else.
3. Let it run 10 minutes untouched.
4. Then send me the dashboard with the hashrate and the accepted / rejected column, plus the first 20 log lines after boot.

The one line I want to see in that log this time is a nonce or an accepted share. If the chip is detected and still returns nothing on a clean factory image with the stock supply, that settles it as hardware and I write it up for you.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Careful, these lines are from the old session, not the new one.

Two tells:

1. The timestamps carry straight on from the log you sent before (685265 then 708194, 735570, 785816), so the uptime counter never restarted. A factory flash plus power cycle resets that to a few thousand.
2. Pool 3 is still configured and still looping on pool.harlolabs.com. A factory image wipes saved settings, so a freshly flashed board would have no pool 3 at all.

So either the board has not been power cycled since the flash, or the browser is showing a cached log page.

Do this:

1. Unplug the XT30 for 30 seconds, plug it back in.
2. Hard refresh the log page (Ctrl + F5) and confirm the timestamps now start low, a few thousand, not 700000.
3. Set pool 1 to your Kryptex BCH entry, leave pool 2 and 3 empty.
4. Ten minutes untouched, then send me the dashboard with hashrate and accepted / rejected, and the first 20 log lines of that new boot.

That new boot log is the one that decides this.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)
